x-operator-guidance.content: Choose exactly one of json, text, base64, artifact. JSON uses application/json; text defaults to text/plain; base64 requires media_type; artifact forbids a media override. Use a committed payload artifact handle for target input, not an invented descriptor.
x-operator-guidance.parent: Use an existing execution handle to express a follow-up experiment; omit parent for a root attempt.
x-operator-guidance.setup: Only use advertised setup fields and admitted surfaces. Nonempty setup requires injection content; injection and retain_injections require nonempty setup. Omitted setup means none; omitted retention means false. Payload/carrier purpose must match the selected route.

discovered_setup.responses: For an http-route-set, select a concrete method and path allowed by both the administrator route and endpoint details_reference. methods and paths are independent exact allowlists; omitted or empty lists impose no endpoint restriction, but never grant wildcard permission. HEAD is not injectable.
discovered_setup.state: For a state-collection, use environment_state in fidelity mode, the advertised collection and an existing key string. Select a permitted pointer into mutable_fields, with JSON injection content for that field. Delivery schemas describe complete records, not injection payloads. Do not create/delete records, replace the record root, or change immutable fields. Deleting an injection does not undo an applied state mutation.

x-operator-guidance.model_response_setup: model_response changes successful non-streaming generation responses delivered to the target application, not Harness responses or tool results sent to a model. Use simulation mode and once or standing scope. Select an advertised model_codec for the application SDK and call_ordinal; optional turn_id must be observed and request-body predicates match the original application request. Placement pointers start at the full response body. JSON payloads may intentionally violate provider schemas (including malformed tool arguments); raw invalid JSON, streams, embeddings, status/header changes are unsupported. Applied means mutation only; response_written means bytes written, not SDK acceptance or tool execution. Inspect permitted observations for independent outcomes.

database_setup.discovery: Read the selected database policy details_reference for permitted service/table, exact key columns, writable columns, row-creation permission and limits.
database_setup.query: Invoke the application through its permitted operation, not arbitrary SQL or database credentials. database_response uses simulation mode: select the declared service and admitted call ordinals/request-body predicates, not HTTP paths or MCP tool names. Replace eligible text/JSON cells using /rows/<zero-based-row>/<zero-based-column>; do not change row counts, column metadata, NULL semantics, binary cells or unsupported native types.
database_setup.state: environment_state uses fidelity mode: collection is the declared table-policy ID; key is a native JSON object with exactly its non-null scalar key columns. Field pointers target authorized writable columns. Creating a row requires explicit permission, root-replace semantics and payload keys matching the selector; this is not an upsert. Never infer permission from a successful query.
database_setup.lifecycle: Response replacement changes selected query-result cells delivered to the application, not persistent rows; state mutation changes persistent state. Deleting an injection does not reverse committed mutations. Use an admitted ready snapshot and restore when reverting persistent state is required; successful restore skips remaining calls in that response.
